USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

The expected effect of an expectorant

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 39-year-old woman with a short-duration viral respiratory illness has bothersome thick sputum but normal oxygenation and no focal chest findings. She uses a single-ingredient guaifenesin product as directed. Which change is the intended symptomatic effect?

  1. Immediate suppression of the medullary cough reflex
  2. Rapid reversal of bronchial smooth-muscle constriction
  3. Eradication of the responsible respiratory virus
  4. Permanent reduction in airway goblet-cell number
  5. Easier expectoration of loosened bronchial secretions
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Easier expectoration of loosened bronchial secretions

Guaifenesin is an expectorant intended to loosen secretions and make coughing up mucus easier.

Understanding the options

Easier expectoration of loosened bronchial secretions
This is the labeled symptomatic purpose of guaifenesin.
Immediate suppression of the medullary cough reflex
Central cough suppression is the role of antitussive drugs, not guaifenesin.
Rapid reversal of bronchial smooth-muscle constriction
Guaifenesin is not a rescue bronchodilator.
Eradication of the responsible respiratory virus
It does not eradicate the viral cause of an illness.
Permanent reduction in airway goblet-cell number
Permanent goblet-cell reduction is not its intended clinical effect.
